```{python}
#| echo: true

# Team Skill Matrix (UPDATED to your 10 skills) + Interactive Visuals
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
import plotly.express as px, plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

# -----------------------------
# 1) Skill levels (1–5) — per your latest notes
# -----------------------------
skills_data = {
    "Name": ["Amogh", "Othmane"],
    # very well (both)
    "Communication": [5, 5],
    # acceptable (both)
    "Data Analysis": [3, 3],
    # Othmane higher
    "Management": [3, 4],
    # doing well (both)
    "SQL": [4, 4],
    # Othmane higher; Amogh very close
    "Problem Solving": [4, 5],
    # doing well (both)
    "Leadership": [4, 4],
    # acceptable (both)
    "Computer Science": [3, 3],
    # Othmane doing well; Amogh slightly above
    "Operations": [5, 4],
    # Othmane doing well; Amogh close
    "Project Management": [3, 4],
    # doing well (both)
    "Business Process": [4, 4],
}

# Optional target levels for Business Analyst roles (1–5)
target_level = {
    "Communication": 5,
    "Data Analysis": 4,
    "Management": 4,
    "SQL": 4,
    "Problem Solving": 4,
    "Leadership": 4,
    "Computer Science": 3,
    "Operations": 4,
    "Project Management": 4,
    "Business Process": 4,
}

# -----------------------------
# 2) Build & validate dataframe
# -----------------------------
df_skills = pd.DataFrame(skills_data).set_index("Name")
df_skills = (
    df_skills.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
             .fillna(1).clip(1, 5).round().astype(int)
)

team_avg = df_skills.mean().rename("Team Avg (1–5)")
summary = pd.concat(
    [team_avg, df_skills.min().rename("Min"), df_skills.max().rename("Max")], axis=1
).sort_values("Team Avg (1–5)", ascending=False)

display(Markdown("### Team Skills — DataFrame (Updated)"))
display(df_skills)
display(Markdown("### Team Summary by Skill"))
display(summary)

# -----------------------------
# 3) Interactive heatmap
# -----------------------------
px.defaults.template = "plotly_white"
px.defaults.width = 980
px.defaults.height = 460

fig_heat = px.imshow(
    df_skills.values,
    x=df_skills.columns, y=df_skills.index,
    color_continuous_scale="Blues", zmin=1, zmax=5,
    labels=dict(color="Level (1–5)")
)
fig_heat.update_layout(
    title=dict(text="Skill Levels (1–5): Amogh & Othmane — Updated", x=0.02),
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=60, b=10),
    xaxis_title="Skill", yaxis_title="Member"
)
fig_heat.update_traces(hovertemplate="Member: %{y}<br>Skill: %{x}<br>Level: %{z}<extra></extra>")
fig_heat.show()

# -----------------------------
# 4) Member comparison bars (dropdown to switch)
# -----------------------------
members = df_skills.index.tolist()
skills  = df_skills.columns.tolist()

def frame_for(member):
    d = pd.DataFrame({
        "Skill": skills,
        member: df_skills.loc[member, skills].values,
        "Team Avg": team_avg[skills].values
    }).sort_values(member, ascending=False)
    return [
        go.Bar(x=d[member], y=d["Skill"], orientation="h", name=member),
        go.Bar(x=d["Team Avg"], y=d["Skill"], orientation="h", name="Team Avg")
    ]

base = members[0]
fig_comp = go.Figure(data=frame_for(base))
fig_comp.update_layout(
    barmode="group",
    title=dict(text=f"Skill Profile — {base} vs Team Avg (Updated)", x=0.02),
    xaxis_title="Level (1–5)", yaxis_title="Skill",
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=60, b=10),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1)
)
fig_comp.frames = [go.Frame(name=m, data=frame_for(m)) for m in members]
fig_comp.update_layout(
    updatemenus=[dict(
        type="dropdown", x=1.0, xanchor="right", y=1.15, yanchor="top",
        buttons=[dict(label=m, method="animate",
                      args=[[m], {"mode":"immediate","fromcurrent":True,
                                  "transition":{"duration":0},
                                  "frame":{"duration":0, "redraw":True}}]) for m in members]
    )]
)
fig_comp.show()

# -----------------------------
# 5) Radar: Team Avg vs Target (exec view)
# -----------------------------
target_series = pd.Series(target_level).reindex(skills).fillna(3).clip(1,5)
radar_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Skill": skills,
    "Team Avg": team_avg.reindex(skills).values,
    "Target": target_series.values
})
cats = radar_df["Skill"].tolist()
team_vals = radar_df["Team Avg"].tolist()
targ_vals = radar_df["Target"].tolist()
cats_closed = cats + [cats[0]]
team_closed = team_vals + [team_vals[0]]
targ_closed = targ_vals + [targ_vals[0]]

fig_radar = go.Figure()
fig_radar.add_trace(go.Scatterpolar(r=team_closed, theta=cats_closed, fill='toself', name='Team Avg'))
fig_radar.add_trace(go.Scatterpolar(r=targ_closed, theta=cats_closed, fill='toself', name='Target'))
fig_radar.update_layout(
    title=dict(text="Skill Radar — Team Avg vs Target (Updated)", x=0.02),
    polar=dict(radialaxis=dict(visible=True, range=[0,5])),
    showlegend=True, height=620,
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=60, b=10)
)
fig_radar.show()

# -----------------------------
# 6) Quick takeaways (auto text)
# -----------------------------
gaps = (target_series - team_avg.reindex(skills)).sort_values(ascending=False)
top_gaps = gaps[gaps > 0]
bullets = [f"- **{s}**: raise by ~{int(np.ceil(g))} level(s) (team avg {team_avg[s]:.1f} vs target {target_series[s]:.1f})"
           for s, g in top_gaps.items()]
display(Markdown("### Quick Takeaways (Updated)"))
display(Markdown("\n".join(bullets) if bullets else "- Team meets or exceeds target across listed skills."))

```

## Team skills Comparison to industry requirements

```{python}

#| echo: true
# Compare Amogh & Othmane to industry requirements (focused skill list)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, re
import plotly.express as px, plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0) Team skill levels (1–5) based on your brief
# ------------------------------------------------------------
skills_data = {
    "Name": ["Amogh", "Othmane"],
    # communication: very well (both)
    "Communication": [5, 5],
    # data analysis: acceptable (both)
    "Data Analysis": [3, 3],
    # management: Othmane higher
    "Management": [3, 4],
    # SQL: doing well (both)
    "SQL": [4, 4],
    # problem solving: Othmane higher, Amogh very close
    "Problem Solving": [4, 5],
    # leadership: both doing well
    "Leadership": [4, 4],
    # computer science: acceptable (both)
    "Computer Science": [3, 3],
    # operations: Othmane doing well; Amogh slightly above
    "Operations": [5, 4],
    # project management: Othmane doing well; Amogh close
    "Project Management": [3, 4],
    # business process: both doing well
    "Business Process": [4, 4],
}
df_skills = pd.DataFrame(skills_data).set_index("Name")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Industry demand for the same skills (from Lightcast)
#    - tries cleaned file first, then raw
#    - parses skills columns and counts exact token matches
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def load_lightcast():
    for p in ["Data/lightcast_clean_final.csv", "Data/lightcast_job_postings.csv"]:
        try:
            return pd.read_csv(p, low_memory=False)
        except Exception:
            pass
    return None

jobs = load_lightcast()
selected_skills = list(df_skills.columns)

def market_counts_from_jobs(jobs_df, selected):
    if jobs_df is None:
        # fallback: equal weights if dataset not available
        return pd.DataFrame({"Skill": selected, "Mentions": [1]*len(selected)})

    skill_cols = [c for c in [
        "SKILLS_NAME","SPECIALIZED_SKILLS_NAME","COMMON_SKILLS_NAME",
        "SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME","JOB_SKILLS","SKILL_NAME"
    ] if c in jobs_df.columns]
    if not skill_cols:
        return pd.DataFrame({"Skill": selected, "Mentions": [1]*len(selected)})

    # build a flat Series of atomic, lowercased skills
    tokens = []
    for c in skill_cols:
        s = (jobs_df[c].dropna().astype(str)
             .str.replace(r"\[|\]", "", regex=True)
             .str.replace('"', "", regex=False)
             .str.replace(r"\\n", " ", regex=True)
             .str.split(r"\s*,\s*|\|"))
        tokens.extend([t.strip().lower() for row in s for t in row if t and t.strip()])

    tok_series = pd.Series(tokens, dtype="string")
    counts = []
    for skill in selected:
        skill_l = skill.lower()
        counts.append(int((tok_series == skill_l).sum()))
    dfm = pd.DataFrame({"Skill": selected, "Mentions": counts})
    # if everything is zero (naming mismatch), give minimal nonzero so visuals still scale
    if dfm["Mentions"].sum() == 0:
        dfm["Mentions"] = 1
    return dfm

df_market = market_counts_from_jobs(jobs, selected_skills)

display(Markdown("### Industry Demand — Top Skills (Lightcast subset)"))
display(df_market.sort_values("Mentions", ascending=False))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Team vs Market alignment table
#    Scale demand to 1–5 so it’s comparable to skill levels
# ------------------------------------------------------------
team_avg = df_skills.mean().rename("Team Avg (1–5)")
df_compare = df_market.merge(team_avg.rename_axis("Skill"), left_on="Skill", right_index=True, how="left")

# scale mentions → 1–5 (robust to constant series)
mmin, mmax = df_compare["Mentions"].min(), df_compare["Mentions"].max()
if mmax == mmin:
    df_compare["Scaled Demand (1–5)"] = 3
else:
    df_compare["Scaled Demand (1–5)"] = (1 + 4*(df_compare["Mentions"]-mmin)/(mmax-mmin)).round(2)

df_compare["Gap (Market - Team)"] = (df_compare["Scaled Demand (1–5)"] - df_compare["Team Avg (1–5)"]).round(2)

display(Markdown("### Team vs Market — Alignment"))
display(df_compare.sort_values("Gap (Market - Team)", ascending=False))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Visualization 1 — Grouped bars (clean executive view)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
fig1 = go.Figure()
fig1.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=df_compare["Skill"], y=df_compare["Scaled Demand (1–5)"],
    name="Industry Demand (scaled)", marker_color="#1f77b4", opacity=0.70
))
fig1.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=df_compare["Skill"], y=df_compare["Team Avg (1–5)"],
    name="Team Average", marker_color="#ff7f0e", opacity=0.90
))
fig1.update_layout(
    title=dict(text="Market Demand vs Team Proficiency (1–5 scale)", x=0.02),
    barmode="group",
    xaxis_tickangle=-35,
    xaxis_title="Skill",
    yaxis_title="Level (1–5)",
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=60, b=120),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1)
)
fig1.show()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Visualization 2 — Bubble chart (demand vs proficiency)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
fig2 = px.scatter(
    df_compare, x="Team Avg (1–5)", y="Scaled Demand (1–5)",
    size="Mentions", color="Gap (Market - Team)",
    hover_name="Skill", text="Skill",
    title="Skill Demand vs Team Proficiency — Gap View",
    color_continuous_scale="RdYlBu_r"
)
fig2.update_traces(
    textposition="top center",
    marker=dict(sizemode="area", line=dict(width=1, color="DarkSlateGrey"))
)
fig2.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Team Average (1–5)",
    yaxis_title="Market Demand (scaled 1–5)",
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=60, b=10),
    height=600
)
fig2.show()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Top gaps (actionable list)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
top_gaps = df_compare.sort_values("Gap (Market - Team)", ascending=False).head(5)[
    ["Skill", "Team Avg (1–5)", "Scaled Demand (1–5)", "Gap (Market - Team)"]
]
display(Markdown("### 🔍 Top 5 Gaps to Prioritize"))
display(top_gaps)

# Quick narrative for BA audience
focus = ", ".join(top_gaps["Skill"].head(3).tolist())
display(Markdown(f"""
**Takeaway:** Team strengths show in **Communication, Leadership, SQL**, and **Business Process**.
Focus upskilling on: **{focus}** to align more tightly with market demand.  
Use short, portfolio-ready artifacts (dashboards, case studies, SQL challenge write-ups) to close gaps fast.
"""))


```


# Improvement plan Proposition

```{python}
#| echo: true

# Improvement plan section: gaps, ownership, roadmap, actions, visuals
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0) Ensure team matrix exists (fallback to latest values)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
try:
    df_skills
except NameError:
    df_skills = pd.DataFrame({
        "Name": ["Amogh", "Othmane"],
        "Communication": [5, 5],
        "Data Analysis": [3, 3],
        "Management": [3, 4],
        "SQL": [4, 4],
        "Problem Solving": [4, 5],
        "Leadership": [4, 4],
        "Computer Science": [3, 3],
        "Operations": [5, 4],
        "Project Management": [3, 4],
        "Business Process": [4, 4],
    }).set_index("Name")

df_skills = (df_skills.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
                        .clip(1,5).round().astype(int))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Targets & gaps (Target − Current, clipped at 0)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
targets = {
    "Communication": 5, "Data Analysis": 4, "Management": 4, "SQL": 4,
    "Problem Solving": 4, "Leadership": 4, "Computer Science": 3,
    "Operations": 4, "Project Management": 4, "Business Process": 4,
}
target_s = pd.Series(targets).reindex(df_skills.columns)
gaps = (target_s - df_skills).clip(lower=0)

display(Markdown("### Individual Skill Gaps (vs. Target)"))
display(gaps.style.background_gradient(cmap="Reds", axis=None))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Priority skills per member (top 3 by gap)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
priority = {}
for member in df_skills.index:
    s = gaps.loc[member]
    priority[member] = s[s>0].sort_values(ascending=False).head(3).index.tolist()

display(Markdown("### Priority Focus per Member"))
for m, skills in priority.items():
    display(Markdown(f"- **{m}** → " + (", ".join(skills) if skills else "meets or exceeds target levels.")))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Team focus and overview chart
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
team_avg_gap = gaps.mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
display(Markdown("### Team Collaboration Focus (Average Gaps)"))
display(team_avg_gap.to_frame("Avg Gap (1–5)"))

fig = px.bar(
    team_avg_gap.reset_index().rename(columns={"index":"Skill", 0:"Avg Gap"}),
    x="Skill", y=team_avg_gap.values,
    title="Average Skill Gaps Across Team (1–5)",
    text=[f"{v:.1f}" for v in team_avg_gap.values],
    color=team_avg_gap.values, color_continuous_scale="Reds", height=450
)
fig.update_traces(textposition="outside")
fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="Skill", yaxis_title="Gap (Target − Current)",
                  margin=dict(l=10,r=10,t=60,b=80))
fig.show()

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Ownership plan for upcoming focus areas
#    - choose skills that need work, ordered by team impact
#    - alternate lead when ties; cap leads per person to keep it even
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
skills_need = team_avg_gap[team_avg_gap > 0].index.tolist()
max_leads = 2  # per person
lead_count = {"Amogh": 0, "Othmane": 0}
last_assigned = None
rows = []

for skill in skills_need:
    a_gap = float(gaps.loc["Amogh", skill])
    o_gap = float(gaps.loc["Othmane", skill])

    if a_gap > o_gap:
        lead, support = "Amogh", "Othmane"
    elif o_gap > a_gap:
        lead, support = "Othmane", "Amogh"
    else:
        # tie → rotate
        lead, support = (("Othmane", "Amogh") if last_assigned == "Amogh"
                         else ("Amogh", "Othmane"))

    # simple cap so leads are spread
    if lead_count[lead] >= max_leads and lead_count[support] < max_leads:
        lead, support = support, lead

    rows.append({
        "Skill": skill,
        "Lead": lead,
        "Support": support,
        "Lead Gap": gaps.loc[lead, skill],
        "Support Gap": gaps.loc[support, skill]
    })
    lead_count[lead] += 1
    last_assigned = lead
    if lead_count["Amogh"] >= max_leads and lead_count["Othmane"] >= max_leads:
        break

df_own = pd.DataFrame(rows)
display(Markdown("### Ownership Plan"))
if len(df_own):
    display(df_own[["Skill","Lead","Support","Lead Gap","Support Gap"]])
else:
    display(Markdown("_No gaps detected across skills._"))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) 4-month roadmap (lead ↔ support rotates on repeats)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
months = ["Month 1","Month 2","Month 3","Month 4"]
plan_rows = []
if len(df_own) == 0:
    plan_rows = [{"Month": m, "Focus Area": "Portfolio Practice",
                  "Lead": "Amogh" if i%2==0 else "Othmane",
                  "Support": "Othmane" if i%2==0 else "Amogh",
                  "Learning Mode": "Pair project & code review",
                  "Expected Outcome": "Publish BA case study"}
                 for i,m in enumerate(months)]
else:
    for i, m in enumerate(months):
        src = df_own.iloc[i % len(df_own)].copy()
        if i >= len(df_own):
            src["Lead"], src["Support"] = src["Support"], src["Lead"]
        plan_rows.append({
            "Month": m,
            "Focus Area": src["Skill"],
            "Lead": src["Lead"],
            "Support": src["Support"],
            "Learning Mode": ("Hands-on mini-project + course" if i == 0 else
                              "Case study & sprint rituals" if i == 1 else
                              "Shadow → swap roles & peer review" if i == 2 else
                              "Stakeholder presentation & retros"),
            "Expected Outcome": ("SQL→BI pipeline & dashboard" if i == 0 else
                                 "Agile board, story map, status report" if i == 1 else
                                 "Documented playbook & SOPs" if i == 2 else
                                 "Executive data story & slide deck")
        })
roadmap = pd.DataFrame(plan_rows)
display(Markdown("### 4-Month Roadmap"))
display(roadmap)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Resources by focus area (BA-oriented)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
resource_map = {
    "Data Analysis": [
        "Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate (Coursera)",
        "Data Visualization with Power BI & Tableau (LinkedIn Learning)",
    ],
    "Management": [
        "Strategic Decision Making (edX)",
        "Leadership Communication (Coursera)",
    ],
    "Project Management": [
        "Google Project Management Certificate (Coursera)",
        "Agile Project Management Foundations (LinkedIn Learning)",
    ],
    "Operations": [
        "Operational Analytics & Process Optimization (edX)",
        "Lean Six Sigma Foundations (Coursera)",
    ],
    "Problem Solving": [
        "Critical Thinking for Business Analysts (Udemy)",
        "Analytical Problem Solving (LinkedIn Learning)",
    ],
}
display(Markdown("### Recommended Courses & Learning Paths"))
for _, r in roadmap.iterrows():
    s = r["Focus Area"]
    if s in resource_map:
        display(Markdown(f"**{s}**"))
        for c in resource_map[s]:
            display(Markdown(f"- {c}"))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) Personal action items 
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
def top_actions(member, n=3):
    s = gaps.loc[member].sort_values(ascending=False)
    real = s[s>0].index.tolist()
    out = real[:n]
    if len(out) < n:
        add = [k for k in team_avg_gap.index if k not in out]
        out.extend(add[:(n-len(out))])
    return out[:n]

amogh_actions = top_actions("Amogh", 3)
othmane_actions = top_actions("Othmane", 3)

display(Markdown("### Personal Action Items"))
display(Markdown(f"- **Amogh** → {', '.join(amogh_actions)}"))
display(Markdown(f"- **Othmane** → {', '.join(othmane_actions)}"))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8) Quick summary
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
display(Markdown(f"""
**Summary**  
Upcoming work is organized by impact areas with clear lead/support roles and a month-by-month plan.
Each member has three concrete action items to convert learning into portfolio-quality outputs.
"""))


```
